explain.say: Here is a simple board. Now, Omar talks, and I listen. Next, my turn. If you forget your idea, you can say, Can I tell you something? Well done! Your challenge: try a catch chat with someone today.

faq.q: How do I know it is my turn?
faq.a: Wait for a pause, when the other person stops talking. Their face might look at you too. Then it is your turn.
asks: Tell me about A little pause
Tell me about Next: my turn

faq.q: How do I show I am listening?
faq.a: Turn towards the person, nod, and say small words like Oh or Really. You do not have to look in their eyes.
asks: Tell me about Now: Omar talks

faq.q: What if I really want to say something?
faq.a: Hold the idea in your head, or squeeze your fingers to keep it. When there is a pause, you can say, Can I tell you something?
asks: Tell me about A big idea

faq.q: What if I talk over someone by mistake?
faq.a: That happens to everyone. You can say, Sorry, you go first. Then listen.

faq.q: How does it feel when someone talks over me?
faq.a: It can feel a bit sad, like your words do not matter. Taking turns helps everyone feel their words matter.

facts: In a conversation, people usually take turns, with short pauses in between.
Nodding is one way to show someone you are listening.
